label: def:frobenius-hopf-substrate
title: The quantum vacuum as a Frobenius--Hopf algebra
html:
Definition. The quantum vacuum as a Frobenius--Hopf algebra

Let \mathbf{C} be a braided monoidal category, with braiding \beta. A Frobenius--Hopf substrate is a sextuple (A, \mu, \eta, \Delta, \varepsilon, S) in \mathbf{C} equipped with a Frobenius form \lambda \colon A \to \mathbf{1} satisfying the following axioms:

  1. Algebra structure: The morphisms \mu \colon A \otimes A \to A and \eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to A make A an associative unital algebra object in \mathbf{C}.

  2. Coalgebra structure and antipode: The morphisms \Delta \colon A \to A \otimes A and \varepsilon \colon A \to \mathbf{1} make A a coassociative counital coalgebra object. The counit is multiplicative, \varepsilon \circ \mu = u \circ (\varepsilon \otimes \varepsilon) with u the canonical unit isomorphism.

    The antipode S \colon A \to A is an involutive anti-automorphism of the whole structure:

\[
\begin{aligned}
  S \circ \mu &= \mu \circ \beta_{A,A} \circ (S \otimes S),
  &\qquad \Delta \circ S &= (S \otimes S) \circ \beta_{A,A} \circ \Delta, \\
  S \circ \eta &= \eta,
  &\qquad \varepsilon \circ S &= \varepsilon, \\
  S \circ S &= \mathrm{id}_A,
  &\qquad \lambda \circ S &= \lambda.
\end{aligned}
\]

In elements the first two read S(ab) = S(b)\,S(a) and \Delta(S x) = \sum S(x_{(2)}) \otimes S(x_{(1)}). The braiding \beta is what makes "reverses" expressible, which is why \mathbf{C} is taken braided; that is no extra demand, since the substrate is invoked at the level of a quantum universe, which is braided monoidal.

S is constrained but not determined. Every classical antipode satisfies these six conditions, and on a non-commutative A they exclude the trivial choice S = \mathrm{id}_A. They do not single S out: the only condition that does is the convolution identity \mu \circ (S \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta = \eta \circ \varepsilon, and that identity forces A to be trivial whenever the scalars form a field, so it cannot be imposed here. 3. Frobenius relation: The Frobenius form \lambda satisfies \mu \circ \Delta = (\Delta \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \alpha \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mu), where \alpha is the associator in \mathbf{C}. 4. Non-degeneracy: Write \mathrm{ev} = \lambda \circ \mu \colon A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1} for the Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_F = \lambda(\mu(a \otimes b)). There is a morphism \mathrm{coev} \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \otimes A such that both snake identities hold:

\[
\begin{aligned}
(\mathrm{id}_A \otimes \mathrm{ev}) \circ (\mathrm{coev} \otimes \mathrm{id}_A) &= \mathrm{id}_A, \\
(\mathrm{ev} \otimes \mathrm{id}_A) \circ (\mathrm{id}_A \otimes \mathrm{coev}) &= \mathrm{id}_A,
\end{aligned}
\]

each read modulo the unitors and the associator of \mathbf{C}.

  1. Self-duality: The pair (\mathrm{ev}, \mathrm{coev}) exhibits A as its own dual. This couples the observer trace \Phi = \lambda \circ \mu to the observed state space intrinsically, and it is what makes the left and right categorical traces on \mathrm{End}(A) available.

Duals are required of A only, not of \mathbf{C}. Axiom 4 supplies \mathrm{coev} as part of the data, so A carries its own duality datum and no object of \mathbf{C} other than A need have a dual. Consequently a Frobenius--Hopf object is available already at the level of a quantum universe, which is braided monoidal but not rigid; rigidity is imposed one level up, on a quantum observable universe, where duals for every object carry the antiparticles and let a strand close into a knot.

An earlier version of this definition opened "Let \mathbf{C} be a rigid monoidal category" and phrased axioms 4--5 as "the induced map A \to A^\vee is an isomorphism". That notation presupposes an ambient dual A^\vee, which made this definition unusable at the level that actually invokes it: def:quantum-universe requires a Frobenius--Hopf object while explicitly stating that rigidity of \mathbf{C} is not required there. The formalization never assumed rigidity either --- FrobeniusHopfData is stated over a bare monoidal category and derives self-duality from \mathrm{coev} plus the snake identities, exactly as axiom 4 now does.
